notes: sort: std slice methods. Go's unstable sort is pdqsort and its order of equal elements is deterministic; where equal elements are distinguishable (Sort, Slice, Float64s) the mapping is rust_stdlib::collections::sort_unstable_by[_less], a port that reproduces it (tests/collections_sort.rs); for integers and strings std's sort_unstable is exact. Go's NaN-first float order is rust_stdlib::math::compare; sort.Interface (Len/Less/Swap over any type) is a slice plus Ord, so the Interface-based entry points collapse into the slice methods.

Find.note: Find(n, cmp) is partition_point over cmp(i) > 0, then an equality check on the found index

Float64s.note: pass rust_stdlib::math::compare for Go's NaN-first order; Go's tie order for -0 and +0

Ints.note: equal integers or strings are indistinguishable, so the order matches Go

Slice.note: less(a, b) on the elements instead of indices; Go's tie order

SliceStable.note: the stable order is unique, so sort_by matches Go

Sort.note: a slice plus a less closure; Go's tie order (the same algorithm as sort.Slice and slices.SortFunc)

Stable.note: the stable order is unique, so sort_by matches Go

Strings.note: equal integers or strings are indistinguishable, so the order matches Go

IntSlice.Sort.note: equal integers or strings are indistinguishable, so the order matches Go

StringSlice.Sort.note: equal integers or strings are indistinguishable, so the order matches Go
